hypothesis: H5, development arm on the frozen candidate's known limit (post-month-end band coverage): not a verdict, does not reopen the candidate unless Eleonora rules so. Do day-specific location and scale terms for the post-month-end business days 1 to 3, read from the calendar position alone and fitted walk-forward, improve the candidate's grid CRPS and upper-tail twCRPS and the coverage of its 90% band on those days?

settled_questions: S18 (#1275, failed) covers a spike-sized carryover term, non-zero only at lead 1 on business day 2. Its 'would reopen it' clause (a business-day split showing the misses concentrate where a location term can act) is met by #1611 and #1614: upper-tail misses on business days 1 and 2 (pooled share 0.166 and 0.144), lower-tail misses on business day 3 (0.151), median error excluding 0 on business day 3. This arm differs from S18 in what it reads and where it acts: no use of the month-end spread (unpublished before business day 2), terms by calendar position alone, acting at every lead, a shift and a scale per group fitted from the group's own earlier cells. #1547's level shift (median z, one pooled group) is the aggregate this splits by business day
candidate: sc_s3c_ann_net, (s3c-ann-net), the walk of candidate_calibration_1363.py unchanged at the 18:00 decision instant, read through scripts/qe_diagnosis_1533.py walk (the same extension as #1533, #1547, #1555 and #1614). No new walk and no refit: each arm is a transform of the candidate's own final quantiles by terms fitted on cells of that walk, so it runs in the cloud, below the long-run line (the walks take about four minutes and the scoring a few)

windows.development: decision days whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31; decides the reading
windows.2026: decision days whose five targets fall from 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03; shown apart, point values, decides nothing. Its terms are fitted from every earlier cell of both windows

groups.meaning: A target day is in a group when `derived_features.bday_of_month` of the target day is 1, 2 or 3 (the count the candidate's post_month_end_window term reads, as #1611 and #1614), and the group is that business day crossed with the kind of the month-end before it: 'quarter' when the target falls in January, April, July or October, else 'other'. Six groups: bd1_quarter, bd2_quarter, bd3_quarter, bd1_other, bd2_other, bd3_other. A day is in exactly one group, so there is no overlap rule. The kind is read from the target date alone: no use of the month-end spread, of the pressure-day type or of any series the decision instant has not published
groups.quarter_ends_apart: The quarter-end month-ends are separate groups because #1614 reads them apart (business day 1 above q95 40 of 145 cells, 0.28, after a quarter-end month-end against 34 of 300, 0.11, after the others). A target day that is itself a quarter-end or year-end day (flag quarter_end, or pressure type quarter_end_turn or year_end) and also falls on business day 1 to 3 is in its group like any other; none is excluded
groups.outside: Every other target day is outside every group: its forecast is the candidate's, the same numbers (the run raises ValueError otherwise)

arms.meaning: Three arms are scored, all declared here, none added later. 'arm' (the primary) applies the group's location shift and the group's two scale factors; 'location' applies the shift only; 'scale' applies the two scale factors only. The candidate's 23 quantiles q_i on a target day in a group become, for every level i: m_i * (q_i - q50) + q50 + delta, with delta the group's shift in bp (0 in the scale arm), m_i the group's lower factor for levels below the median and the upper factor above it (1 in the location arm), and m_median = 1. The median moves by delta alone. The order of the quantiles is kept (a positive factor and one common shift)
arms.cap: Where the candidate's SRF cap bound on a cell (some level has q_i != raw_i; the walk file does not carry the line itself), no arm quantile on that cell is above the largest capped value, so the arm cannot undo the cap. Where it did not bind, the arm is not capped (the line is not in the walk file). This is declared as a limit
arms.reading_order: The primary reading is the 'arm' row. The two components are shown to say which of the two terms carries the difference; neither is a separate hypothesis and no combination of them is searched

fit.location: The median of y - q50_raw over the group's training cells, in bp, where q50_raw is the candidate's raw (pre-cap) median at the cell's lead; the same statistic as #1614's median error, on the raw median, as #1555 fits on raw quantiles and applies to final ones. One shift per group, common to the five leads
fit.scale: #1533's section 2b ratio (scripts/qe_diagnosis_1533.py shape_ratios) on the group's usable training cells (q95_raw > q05_raw): z = (y - q50)/(q95 - q05) on the raw quantiles; ratio_tau is the realised distance of the tail from the median (the sample quantile tau of z less the sample median of z) over the law's distance. The lower factor is built from ratio_0.05, the upper from ratio_0.95. The statistic is a distance from the median of z, so it does not depend on the shift. One pair of factors per group, common to the five leads
fit.training_cells: At a decision day d, the cells of the group, at every lead, whose target day is strictly before d, from both windows in date order (the first decision day has none). The 5 cells of a decision day share one fit. A cell whose target day is d or later is never read; the run raises LookAheadError if it is. This is #1555's rule
fit.shrinkage: With n the group's usable training cells and k = 100 cells (about 20 target days at five leads): delta = n / (n + k) * median_error and m = 1 + n / (n + k) * (ratio - 1). With fewer than 50 usable training cells (MIN_TRAIN, about 10 target days), or a median that is not finite, delta = 0, and a ratio that is not a positive finite number gives m = 1. k = 100 and the minimum of 50 are this study's choice, smaller than #1555's (500 and 100) because a group holds at most about 300 development cells; they are fixed here before any score, and no other value is run. The choice is a question for Eleonora in the pull request
fit.no_other_fit: No grid of k, no per-lead or per-regime term, no timing term that reads the month-end spread, no other group definition and no other tail level is tried. The sizes come from the walk, not from #1612's or #1614's point values

protocol.pooled: Grid CRPS and upper-tail twCRPS, one score per decision day (the mean over its five leads, as scoring_protocol.day_scores), each arm against the candidate and the primary arm against B1, B1' and B2 (and the candidate against them), on scoring protocol v1's studentized stationary bootstrap (repo_model.scoring_protocol.paired_tests: mean block 10, 10000 draws, HAC lag 10, seed 1615, one resample stream for all pairs), over every decision day of the development window. The figure is the mean of d = S(reference) - S(arm), positive favours the arm, with a two-sided 90% interval read from the studentized draws as the point less the 0.95 and 0.05 quantiles of the t-draws times the HAC standard error. Skill is not reported. Only 'the share of cells changed' of this pooled figure is on post-month-end days, so it is diluted by the days the arm leaves alone; the window rows below carry the effect
protocol.splits: The same paired differences (d for grid CRPS and twCRPS against the candidate, B1, B1' and B2 for the primary arm; each arm against the candidate) and the strict miss rates below q05 and above q95, for the post-month-end window as a whole (every group), by business day (1, 2, 3), by business day crossed with the kind (the six groups), by regime of the target day, by lead, and by regime within the window; the interval is the stationary bootstrap of the target days of the rows in date order (mean block 10, 1000 resamples, seed 1615, every cell of a drawn day comes with it), the 90% percentile interval, as #1555. A split with fewer than 30 cells is 'too few'
protocol.coverage: The 90% band's strict miss rate below q05 and above q95 against the nominal 0.05, per business day and per group, the candidate and each arm, with the same interval
protocol.terms: The terms the walk gave: for each group and arm term, its value at the first decision day of each year and at the last of the window, and its range
protocol.2026: Shown apart as point values on the 2026 window: the window rows and the six groups. They decide nothing

reading.window_loss: The primary arm loses on the post-month-end window when its mean grid CRPS over the development window's cells in a group is not below the candidate's (mean d <= 0, d the candidate's score less the arm's); it wins when the two-sided 90% interval of d (the target-day stationary bootstrap) lies wholly above 0; between the two it is undecided. The same reading is made on the pooled protocol figure. The pull request marks both as questions for Eleonora. Only a loss on the window adds a settled-questions entry closing the line
reading.no_verdict: Development data on seen days, and the business days and the kind were chosen after #1612 and #1614 read these misses from the same window, so the figures flatter the arm. Nothing here is a verdict, and the arm does not change the frozen candidate

provisional: The arms train on the candidate's own walk (direct pairs, calendar read at the target day); they call no guarded fitter, so they are not a producer for docs/research/provisional-calendar-register.md
limits: development data on seen days, never a verdict; the 2026 days are shown apart and decide nothing
the groups were chosen from the same development window by #1611 and #1614 (selection on the sample the arm is scored on), so the development figures are optimistic for the arm
k = 100 and the minimum of 50 cells are choices; the early decision days of a group have a term of 0 or a heavily shrunk one
the fit reads the raw quantiles and the arm transforms the final ones (50 development cells differ, #1555); the cap is kept only where it bound
a group has 29 (quarter) or 60 (other) development target days per business day: the intervals on a single group are wide

variants.arm: the primary: shift and both factors
variants.candidate: the unchanged candidate, read from the same walk
